title: Gizemler
canDo: Elimdeki ipuçlarından yola çıkarak must, might, may, could ve can't ile şu anki durumlar hakkında çıkarım yapabilir, ne kadar emin olduğumu ifade edebilir ve gizem ve suç kelimeleriyle bir olayı tartışabilirim.
grammar: emin olma dereceleri: definitely, probably, perhaps

liveClass.title: Dedektif masası
liveClass.goal: Gruplar bir "gizem dosyası" alır: Kayıp bir tablo, birkaç şüpheli ve ipuçları (bir fiş, bir ayak izi, bir mesaj). It must be..., It can't be..., He might be... kalıplarıyla şüphelileri tartışır, ne kadar emin olduklarını belirtir ve suçluyu kanıtlarıyla birlikte sınıfa açıklarlar. Doğru çözüme ulaşan grup kazanır.

learn.explanation:
**Çıkarım (deduction)**, elimizdeki **kanıtlara** bakarak bir şeyin **doğru olup olmadığı** hakkında tahmin yürütmektir.

| Modal | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **must** + fiil | **Eminim ki doğru** (%95) | He **must be** a student. (Öğrenci olmalı.) |
| **can't** + fiil | **Eminim ki doğru değil** (%95) | He **can't be** far away. (Uzakta olamaz.) |

**Kanıt → Sonuç:**

- She's wearing a uniform. → She **must be** a nurse.
- He's only 15. → He **can't be** a teacher.
- The lights are off. → They **must be** asleep.

**Dikkat:**

- must'ın olumsuzu çıkarımda **mustn't değil, can't**'tir. (~~He mustn't be at home.~~ → He **can't be** at home.)
- mustn't = **yasak** anlamındadır (A2'de öğrendik).
- Bu kullanımda must zorunluluk anlatmaz.

examples.en: You've been travelling all day. You must be tired.
That can't be Ali. He's in London this week.
examples.tr: O Ali olamaz. Bu hafta Londra'da.

examples.en: This bag must cost a fortune!

learn.turkishNote: Türkçedeki "-malı / -meli" eki hem zorunluluk (gitmelisin) hem çıkarım (yorgun olmalısın) anlatır; İngilizcede de must ikisini de karşılar. Ama olumsuz çıkarımda "olamaz" için can't kullanılır: "O olamaz" → It can't be him. "It mustn't be him" yanlıştır.

lessons.title: Belki de...
lessons.goal: Emin olmadığım durumlar için might, may ve could ile olasılık bildirebilirim.

discover.title: Tavan arasındaki ses
discover.body:
Every night at about midnight, the Aydın family hear a strange noise above their bedroom. It sounds like small footsteps.

Mr Aydın thinks it might be a mouse. "It could be a bird too," he says. "The roof is old, and there may be a hole somewhere."

Their daughter, Ela, has a different idea. "It might be a ghost!" she says. "The house is a hundred years old."

Mrs Aydın doesn't agree. "It can't be a ghost. Ghosts don't exist! And it can't be a bird, because birds sleep at night. It must be a cat from the neighbourhood. I've seen one on the roof."

The family have called an expert, who is coming on Friday to look.

questions.prompt: What does Ela think the noise is?
Why does Mrs Aydın think it can't be a bird?
options: There are no birds in the city.

learn.explanation:
**Emin değilsek** (yaklaşık %30–60):

| Modal | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **might** + fiil | It **might be** a mouse. |
| **may** + fiil | There **may be** a hole in the roof. |
| **could** + fiil | It **could be** a bird. |

Üçü de **"olabilir, belki"** anlamındadır. **may** biraz daha resmîdir.

**Olumsuz:**

- **might not** / **may not** = belki değildir
  - He **might not** know the answer.
- **couldn't** = olamaz (can't gibi), "belki değil" anlamında kullanılmaz!

**Emin olma ölçeği:**

```
%100  It IS a cat.
 %95  It MUST be a cat.
 %50  It MIGHT / MAY / COULD be a cat.
 %50  It MIGHT NOT / MAY NOT be a cat.
 %95  It CAN'T be a cat.
  %0  It ISN'T a cat.
```

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It might rain later.
She may not be at home. Call her mobile.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçedeki "olabilir" ve "olmayabilir" ifadeleri might / may / could ve might not / may not ile karşılanır. "couldn't" ise "olmayabilir" değil, "olamaz" anlamına gelir. "Evde olmayabilir" → She might not be at home (~~She couldn't be at home~~).

options: She might not be at home.

learn.explanation:
Birinin **şu anda** ne yaptığı hakkında çıkarım yaparken **modal + be + -ing** kullanılır:

| Yapı | Anlam | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **must be** + -ing | şu an yapıyor **olmalı** | He **must be sleeping**. |
| **might / may / could be** + -ing | şu an yapıyor **olabilir** | He **might be driving**. |
| **can't be** + -ing | şu an yapıyor **olamaz** | He **can't be driving**. |

**Karşılaştırın:**

- He **must be** tired. (Durum → be + sıfat)
- He **must be sleeping**. (Şu anki eylem → be + -ing)
- He **must sleep** a lot. (Genel alışkanlık → yalın fiil)

**Sık kullanılan kalıplar:**

- **You must be joking!** (Şaka yapıyor olmalısın!)
- **They must be having fun.**
- **She can't be working**; it's Sunday.

lessons.title: Dedektif kelimeleri
lessons.goal: Suç ve dedektiflik kelimeleriyle bir olayı ve ipuçlarını anlatabilirim.

discover.title: Müzedeki hırsızlık
discover.body:
Last night, a burglar broke into a small museum in Safranbolu and stole a valuable old clock.

Detective Ayla Şen arrived early this morning. "There are no fingerprints, so the thief must be an expert," she said. "But there are footprints in the garden. They're quite small, so the suspect might be a woman, or a man with small feet."

The police are questioning three suspects: the night guard, a cleaner and a visitor who was in the museum yesterday afternoon. The night guard has an alibi. A witness saw him at a café at the time of the crime.

"The guard can't be guilty," says the detective. "But someone knew the code for the alarm. That's an important clue."

questions.prompt: Why does the detective think the thief must be an expert?
questions.explanation: "There are no fingerprints, so the thief must be an expert"

questions.prompt: Why can't the night guard be guilty?

learn.explanation:
**Suç ve dedektiflik kelimeleri:**

| Kişiler | Eylemler | Kanıtlar |
|---|---|---|
| **detective** (dedektif) | **steal** (çalmak) | **clue** (ipucu) |
| **suspect** (şüpheli) | **break into** (zorla girmek) | **evidence** (kanıt) |
| **witness** (tanık) | **solve** (çözmek) | **fingerprint** (parmak izi) |
| **burglar** (eve giren hırsız) | **question** (sorgulamak) | **footprint** (ayak izi) |
| **thief** (hırsız) | **arrest** (tutuklamak) | **alibi** (mazeret) |

**steal mi rob mu?**

- **steal** + **eşya**: They **stole** a clock / my phone.
- **rob** + **kişi / yer**: They **robbed** a bank / an old man.

**Sıfatlar:** **guilty** (suçlu) ↔ **innocent** (masum)

**Çıkarımla birleştirme:**

- There are no fingerprints, **so** the thief **must** be an expert.
- He has an alibi, **so** he **can't** be guilty.
- The footprints are small, **so** the suspect **might** be a woman.

learn.explanation:
Modallar dışında da **ne kadar emin olduğumuzu** gösterebiliriz:

| Kesinlik | İfadeler |
|---|---|
| **Çok emin** | I'm sure / certain (that) ... / It's **definitely** ... / **There's no doubt** that ... |
| **Oldukça emin** | It's **probably** ... / I **think** ... / It's **likely** that ... |
| **Emin değil** | **Perhaps / Maybe** ... / It's **possible** that ... / I'm **not sure**. |
| **Pek inanmıyor** | I **doubt** it. / I'm **not convinced**. / It's **unlikely** that ... |
| **Kesinlikle hayır** | It's **definitely not** ... / There's **no way** ... |

**Yer:** definitely / probably genellikle **be'den sonra**, diğer fiillerden **önce** gelir:

- It's **probably** a gas. / He **probably** knows.

**Fikir tartışmak:**

- **Personally**, I think ... / **In my opinion**, ...
- **That's possible, but** ... / **I'm not sure about that.**
- **Me too. / Me neither. / I think so too.**

task.prompt: Bir forumda gerçek ya da hayali bir gizem hakkında yazın (130–160 kelime): Ne oldu, ipuçları neler, insanlar ne düşünüyor? Farklı teorileri must / might / could / can't ile tartışın, definitely / probably / I doubt it gibi ifadelerle ne kadar emin olduğunuzu belirtin ve kendi teorinizi açıklayın.
task.modelAnswer:
The Mystery of the Moving Bench

In our park, there's an old wooden bench next to the lake. For the last month, people have noticed something strange: every morning, the bench is in a different place.

Some children say it must be a ghost. I doubt it! Others think it might be teenagers who come to the park at night. That's possible, but the bench is very heavy, so it can't be just one person.

The park gardener has a different idea. He says the city workers could be moving it to clean the grass. But the city says they don't work at night, so that's unlikely.

Personally, I think the answer is probably simple. There's a café next to the park, and the owner is always complaining that the bench is too far from his door. I'm not sure, but I think he might be moving it every night!

Bu gizemi açıklamaya çalışan bir paragraf yazın (120–150 kelime). must, might, could, can't, be + -ing yapıları ve definitely / probably / I doubt gibi kesinlik ifadeleri kullanın.
questions.modelAnswer: This morning I found a small box outside my door. Inside, there was a key, a train ticket to Izmir and a note: "Thank you for everything. – K." Who could it be from? It can't be from my brother, because his name is Murat. It might be from my old flatmate, Kader. She moved to Izmir last year, and she probably wants me to visit her. The key could be for her new flat! But I doubt it, because she always sends messages, not notes. It might be from my neighbour, Kemal Bey. I helped him a lot when he was ill. Perhaps he's moving to Izmir and he wants me to take care of his house. I'm not sure, but there's definitely a story here. Kemal Bey must be at home now, so I'm going to knock on his door and ask!
